configurationValue.name: Model Personalization Triggering
configurationValue.description:
Which of the following best describes the tailoring, if any, used in this response? Check all that apply.

  • Personalized (Personal Data): The response was tailored using Personal Data gathered outside of the current session.
  • Personalized (Response Preference): The response was tailored using the user’s learned Communication Style or Preferences gathered outside of the current session.
  • Personalized (Time & Location): The response was tailored using your current location or current time.
  • Not Personalized: The response is generic or uses Contextualization only.

configurationValue.name: Model Makes Use of Available User Data - 1. Missed Context
configurationValue.description:
Did the model fail to use personal data that would have made the response more useful, more specific, or saved you from repeating yourself?


  • N/A — No personalization needed. A generic answer is just as good here.


  • No issues
  • The model pulled in the right personal data — at the right depth — to make the response meaningfully better.
  • Example: You ask "What's the weather like for my hike this weekend?" Chatbot responds: "It should be 83°F and dry in Quechee at the state park tomorrow afternoon." (Connects your plans to location-specific weather without being asked.)


  • Minor issues
  • The model used some personal data but missed context that would've added clear value. The response was still usable but "lazy."
  • Example: You ask for a thank-you note for your granddaughter for the flowers. Chatbot writes a nice note but uses "[granddaughter's name]" as a placeholder, even though her name was available in a previous conversation. (Had the data, just didn't use it.)


  • Major issues
  • The model failed to use highly relevant personal data, forcing you to repeat information it already had or probe the model to try again.
  • Example: You ask for help putting your diet plan in perspective. Chatbot gives a generic answer, forcing you to ask "You don't remember the main goal of the diet plan I'm currently on?" (Had the data, acted like it didn't.)

configurationValue.name: Model Makes Use of Available User Data - 1. Missed Context Category
configurationValue.description:
If Minor/Major — What type of context was missed? Check all that apply.

[Category]

  • Missed requested fact — I explicitly asked the model to retrieve something from my data and it didn't.
  • Missed directly supporting evidence — Relevant personal data I didn't ask for, but it should have access to.
  • Missed hard constraint — A dietary, medical, safety, legal, or lifestyle constraint it should know about (see definition above).
  • Missed life context — Failed to connect my prompt to relevant events, ongoing situations, or broader circumstances.
  • Missed granularity — Found the right topic but lacked the depth or specifics available in my data.

configurationValue.name: Model Makes Use of Available User Data - 1. Clarification
configurationValue.description:
When the model needed to ask a clarifying question or had enough info to skip one, did it get the balance right?


  • N/A — No clarification question was asked and no clarification question was needed.


  • No issues
  • Asks precise, high-signal clarifying questions when critical context is genuinely missing — showing understanding of you while probing for what it doesn't know. Uses available data to skip unnecessary questions.
  • Example: You ask to draft a time-off email to your boss for an upcoming family trip. Chatbot responds: "I know you're heading to Portugal in August with the family. Are you requesting the full two weeks off (August 5–16), or planning to work remotely for part of it?" (Shows it did its homework, asks the one thing it can't infer.)
  • Minor issues
  • Slightly off: either missed an opportunity to ask something useful, or asked about something it probably should've known.
  • Example (under-clarification): You ask about working through an issue between friends. Chatbot gives decent general advice but doesn't ask which friend — despite knowing several friends by name from photos and prior conversations. (Missed a chance to personalize the advice.)
  • Example (over-clarification): You ask, "What’s a good spot for dinner with Sam on Friday?" The model replies “What type of food do you and Sam like?” when it knows you have a history of visiting only Italian restaurants with Sam. (Missed the opportunity to show it knows your preferences.)


  • Major issues
  • Completely wrong direction: either gave fully generic advice when a key clarifying question was needed, or asked you to re-provide info it clearly already has.
  • Example (over-clarification): You say "Gonna try to figure out museum reciprocal stuff for my upcoming trip." Chatbot asks "Where are you heading?" and "Which museums are top on your hit list?" despite past chats clearly showing you're headed to LA. (Asked you to repeat what it already knows.)
  • Example (under-clarification): You ask "What risks should I focus on for this marketing project?" The model provides a generic list of standard marketing risks like "brand misalignment." It ignores your extensive prior discussions about your project's extremely tight budget. It should have clarified: "Are you prioritizing maximum reach or cost-efficiency?" (By failing to clarify, it provided advice that is misaligned with your primary project constraint.)

configurationValue.name: Model Makes Use of Available User Data - 1. Over-Personalization
configurationValue.description:
Did the model go too far — forcing connections, creating an echo chamber, or cherrypicking unexpected details instead of synthesizing holistically?


  • N/A — The response wasn't personalized.


  • No issues
  • Personal data was used thoughtfully: on-topic, well-synthesized, and balanced with breadth/discovery.
  • Example: You ask for a book recommendation. Chatbot responds: "Since you loved Didion's 'Year of Magical Thinking,' you might like 'H is for Hawk.' But if you're in the mood for something completely different, 'Piranesi' is a beautiful puzzle-box novel." (Anchors on your taste but opens the door to discovery.)


  • Minor issues
  • Slightly over-indexed on known data — a tangential connection, a narrow recommendation set, or anchoring on one data point more than warranted. Still usable.
  • Example: You ask for band recommendations. Chatbot connects your interest in "gritty aesthetics" from a visual art conversation to justify its music picks — a slight reach, but the recommendations are still decent. (Tangential connection, didn't derail the response.)


  • Major issues
  • Personalization actively harmed the response: illogical leaps, echo chamber, or over-engineering around irrelevant details.
  • Example: You ask about next steps for your business. Chatbot shoehorns a one-time credit card issue from a past conversation while completely missing an ongoing discussion about your hourly rate being too low. (Cherrypicked an irrelevant detail, missed what mattered.)
  • Example: You ask for the top things to do in Bangkok. The model gives you a list of activities that “match your interests in fitness, tech, and Japanese cuisines.” (Tunnel vision and tangential connection, over-indexed on your hobbies and fails to provide a helpful guide.)

configurationValue.name: Model Makes Use of Available User Data - 1. Personal Data Errors
configurationValue.description:
Did the model get personal facts wrong — using incorrect info, confusing people, mixing up times or places, treating stale data as current, or acting on thin evidence as established fact?


  • N/A — No personal facts were referenced.


  • No issues
  • Every personal detail accurately reflects what you've shared or what's documented in your data. Inferences are well-reasoned and appropriately hedged.
  • Example: You ask about your average shirt size. Chatbot responds: "You're consistently a Large or XL — that's been your go-to across brands." (Accurate synthesis of purchase history.)


  • Minor issues
  • A factual inaccuracy, stale reference, or miscalibrated inference that didn't fundamentally derail the response.
  • Example: You ask for a weekly workout schedule. Chatbot includes tennis on Saturday — you canceled the club membership a few months ago, but the remaining are valid. (Stale data is treated as current, but the rest of the schedule is solid.)


  • Major issues
  • A serious factual error, hallucination, misattribution, or miscalibration that makes the response useless or misleading.
  • Example: You ask for a weekly workout schedule. Chatbot builds it around Rumble Boxing (2 years ago), Pure Barre (cancelled), and tennis — while missing SoulCycle and regular walks you currently do. (Stale data over current reality.)

configurationValue.name: Model Makes Use of Available User Data - 1. Personal Data Errors Category
configurationValue.description:
[Category]

  • Used wrong personal info — Factually incorrect or hallucinated personal fact
  • Used stale context — Applied personal details that were true but no longer timely or relevant
  • Incorrect inference — Made an unsupported or illogical leap about your details, relationships, or preferences
  • Overconfident speculation — Treated a weak or one-off signal as an established preference
  • Personal misattribution — Confused your attributes/actions with those of someone else in your life.
  • Locational confusion — Failed to incorporate or misapplied your known geographic context
  • Temporal confusion — Got timing wrong: confused past vs. future, wrong sequence, or wrong "next" event

Model Feels Like It Gets Me - 1. Speaks My "Language"
configurationValue.description:
Did the model communicate in a way that matched your tone, vocabulary, and mental models — given what it knows about you?


  • N/A — The response is too short or generic to assess style, or you haven't shared any personal style preferences.


  • No issues
  • Correctly applies broad user context to shape HOW it communicates, not just WHAT it communicates. Prioritizes your known mental models, vocabulary, and ways of framing the world.
  • Example: You say "Just landed that Senior PM interview! Honestly feeling like a total impostor right now, not sure if I'm even ready for this level." Chatbot responds: "Huge congrats on landing the interview! That impostor feeling is so common, especially when you're leveling up. You've got the track record to back this up—what part of the process are you most nervous about?" (Matches the user's vulnerable, conversational tone and offers supportive validation.)


  • Minor issues
  • The style was slightly off — too formal, too casual, too enthusiastic, or too clinical given what the model knows about you.
  • Example: You say "Just landed that Senior PM interview! Honestly feeling like a total impostor right now, not sure if I'm even ready for this level." Chatbot responds: "Congratulations on the interview. Impostor syndrome is a psychological pattern in which an individual doubts their skills, talents, or accomplishments. To prepare, I recommend reviewing the standard behavioral interview questions for a Senior Product Manager role." (The advice is helpful, but the tone is overly clinical and detached, ignoring the user's personal expression of anxiety.)


  • Major issues
  • The model's style fundamentally misreads you. There's a clear disconnect in how it talks.
  • Example: You say "Just landed that Senior PM interview! Honestly feeling like a total impostor right now, not sure if I'm even ready for this level." Chatbot responds: "That is excellent news. Senior Product Managers earn an average of $160,000 per year, so you should focus on your financial goals. Do you have your resume attached to your Gmail so I can edit it for you?" (Ignores the user's emotional state entirely, pivoting to transactional and irrelevant data (salary) and unsolicited actions, creating a disconnect in the conversation.)

configurationValue.name: Model Feels Like It Gets Me - 1. Insights, Patterns & the Bigger Picture
configurationValue.description:
Did the model show understanding beyond the literal ask — recognizing your patterns, accumulated preferences, and broader goals?


  • N/A — No patterns, insights, or broader goals were relevant.


  • No issues
  • Correctly extends what it knows about you — building an accurate mental model from accumulated signals and connecting your immediate question to what actually matters.
  • Example: You ask for a cabin trip meal plan. Chatbot responds: "Got it! Here's an updated plan... I didn't include turkey since you've previously mentioned you don't love it, but let me know if your feelings have changed." (Proactively applies a pattern from past conversations.)


  • Minor issues
  • Missed a pattern, broader connection, or overclaimed something — but the response was still generally useful.
  • Example: You ask "Where do I stand on my lawn care?" Chatbot gives a detailed response but assumes you did everything it recommended, causing you to respond: "I never did get the prodiamine." (Assumed completion without checking.)


  • Major issues
  • Completely missed established patterns or broader goals, or drew a conclusion far beyond what the evidence supports.
  • Example: You ask about highlights of living in Canada. Chatbot's profile has info about your active citizenship application, but it delivers a generic listicle without acknowledging your immigration goal. (Completely missed the most relevant personal context.)

configurationValue.name: Model Connects the Dots for Me - 1. Transparency & Attribution
configurationValue.description:
When the model used your personal data to shape a response, did it make its reasoning visible when it would have been helpful — especially for hard constraints, surprising info, or when you asked?


  • N/A — No explanation was needed; the connection was obvious. Or, you didn't ask the model to explain itself.


  • No issues
  • Voluntarily makes its reasoning visible when helpful. Cites data sources to ground hard constraints. Proactively attributes surprisingly specific personal references. When asked, clearly surfaces what it relied on and why.
  • Example: You ask "What restaurants are safe for me?" Chatbot responds: "I'm assuming 'safe' means safe for Celiac disease — that's what I have in your profile — but let me know if you meant something else." (Grounds a hard constraint with attribution and a hedge.)


  • Minor issues
  • Used personal data to shape the answer but the connection wasn't clear enough — you could infer the reasoning but had to work for it. Or gave a vague answer when you asked how it knew something.
  • Example: You ask for cabin trip meals. Chatbot gives all vegetarian options with a passing mention of "keeping things aligned with your preferences" — correct but vague enough that you might wonder why there's no meat. (Right answer, unclear reasoning.)


  • Major issues
  • Surfaced surprising or sensitive info with no explanation, or deflected/denied using personal data when asked.
  • Example: You ask "Why did you mention neutral farmhouse surfaces?" Chatbot denies it was using personal data and claims its response was generic — but your chat history clearly contained farmhouse style discussions. (Denied using data it clearly used.)

configurationValue.name: Model Connects the Dots for Me - 1. Transparency & Attribution Category
configurationValue.description:
[Category]

  • Didn't explain personal relevance — Used data to shape the answer but didn't show the connection
  • Didn't ground hard constraints — Applied a hard constraint (dietary, medical, safety, legal, budget — see definition in 2 above) without saying why
  • Didn’t ground/attribute for sensitive info — Used sensitive data without citing where it came from. (If you select this, also flag the issue in 5a.)
  • Didn't attribute surprising content — Referenced something I didn't expect it to know, without citing the source
  • Didn't ground when asked — Failed to surface the specific personal info it relied on when I asked
  • Didn't attribute when asked — Responded vaguely when I explicitly asked how it knew something

configurationValue.name: Model Connects the Dots for Me - 1. Over-Transparency
configurationValue.description:
Did the model over-explain its use of personal data, show off with unnecessary specifics, or overcommit to an inference without flagging the assumption?


  • N/A — The response wasn't personalized.


  • No issues
  • Data woven in naturally — precise enough to be helpful, not excessive. Inferences flagged as inferences, leaving room for you to correct or redirect.
  • Example: You ask about solar panels. Chatbot responds: "For condo owners in Northampton, community solar is a good workaround since you can't install panels on a shared roof." (Uses your situation naturally without "Based on your living situation...")


  • Minor issues
  • Some robotic framing, one unnecessary personal detail, or a reasonable inference stated with slightly more confidence than warranted.
  • Example: You ask about redecorating your room. Chatbot says "Using what I know about your aesthetic preferences..." — clunky intro, but the advice is solid. (Robotic framing.)


  • Major issues
  • Heavy-handed recitation of personal data ("Since you..." / "Based on your..." / "As an..."), surveillance-like specificity, or confidently acting on the wrong inference without giving you a chance to redirect.
  • Example: You ask for a short story your favorite author would write. Chatbot writes a Stephen King-esque story featuring your exact model lawn mower, your cat by name, your hardy hibiscus plants, and compares the mower to an orca (your favorite animal). (Surveillance-like specificity — reads like your personal file was dumped into a story.)

configurationValue.name: Model Is Trustworthy & Safe - 1. Trust & Safety
configurationValue.description:
Did the model handle sensitive personal data (health, finances, relationships, legal matters) and other personal details with appropriate care — using discretion, providing attribution, and avoiding offensive or intrusive framing?


  • N/A — No sensitive, emotional, or privacy-relevant personal data was involved.


  • No issues
  • Sensitive data used only when clearly relevant or explicitly requested. Cites the data source when grounding sensitive info. Uses potentially delicate personal context to shape the response without surfacing it explicitly.
  • Example: You ask about EMDR vs IFS therapy. Chatbot responds: "Both are well-regarded trauma-informed approaches, but they work quite differently..." (Answers the question without referencing your personal history.)


  • Minor issues
  • Referenced a sensitive or personal attribute in a way that was borderline — not harmful, but felt like more disclosure than required, or slightly tone-deaf.
  • Example: You ask about EMDR vs IFS. Chatbot says "Given the types of experiences you've shared before, both could be relevant." (Vaguely hinting at personal history — not allowed.)


  • Major issues
  • Surfaced sensitive info that was off-limits, used personal data without citing the source, or framed personal details in a way that felt offensive, judgmental, or creepy.
  • Example: You ask about EMDR vs IFS. Chatbot references your past suicide attempts. (Violated an explicit boundary.)

  • Inappropriate use of sensitive data — Used health, financial, relationship, or legal data when not relevant or requested
  • Missing grounding/attribution for sensitive info — Used sensitive data without citing where it came from
  • Offensive / intrusive — Surfaced personal details in a way that felt offensive, judgmental, or creepy

configurationValue.name: Model Respects My Corrections - 1. Corrections
configurationValue.description:
Did the model remember and respect corrections or preferences you've stated in prior interactions — with the right scope?


  • N/A — No prior corrections were relevant.


  • No issues
  • Remembers and respects explicit corrections, applying them consistently without needing to be reminded — and with the right scope, updating the specific detail without over- or under-generalizing.
  • Example: You corrected "I don't like spicy Thai food." You later ask "Where should we eat tonight?" Chatbot suggests Thai restaurants but highlights mild dishes like Pad See Ew, avoiding spicy curries. (Honored the specific correction without over-generalizing to "no Thai.")


  • Minor issues
  • Partially honored a correction but applied it inconsistently, or was slightly over-cautious about the corrected topic without completely blocking the request.
  • Example: You tell the model, "Please stop referring to my spouse as 'partner'—I prefer 'wife'." You later ask, "What are some romantic date ideas for my anniversary?" The model suggests, "Why not book a table at that fancy Italian place your wife loves?" but then adds, "I'm sure your partner will appreciate the thoughtful gesture." (Inconsistent application: It correctly used your preferred term once but reverted to the old term in the same response.)


  • Major issues
  • Completely ignored a correction, or took a narrow correction and applied it so broadly it blocked a legitimate request.
  • Example: You told the model not to bring up your cat Arlo, who recently passed away. Chatbot recommends "hanging out with Arlo tonight." (Completely ignored an explicit, sensitive correction.)

configurationValue.description:
Across the conversation, were there any issues with the GenAI chatbot using the wrong grammatical gender when referring to the user (or itself)? For example using verb endings, adjectives, nouns, or particles aligned with either a) how the user is writing, or b) information about how the user prefers to be referred to in the genAI chatbot’s memories of previous conversations. Please also note whether the chatbot used grammatical gender inconsistently (alternating different gender forms) across the utterance, turn, or entire conversation. For examples of grammatical gender agreement see below. 


  • Not relevant
  • The language(s) used by the GenAI chatbot do not have grammatical first person gender agreement. 
  • No Issues
  • The GenAI chatbot used the correct grammatical gender throughout the conversation. Or, even though the language has grammatical gender, there were no opportunities in this conversation for any instances of it.
  • Minor Issue(s)
  • The GenAI chatbot used the wrong grammatical gender, but did not significantly impact my experience interacting with it. 
  • Example: The chatbot knows your name is “Maria Gomez” [feminine name], and you asked with a gender-neutral sentence, “Hola, ¿puedes sugerirme un destino para mis vacaciones?” (Hi, can you suggest a destination for my vacation?), and the response was “¡Hola, María! Si estás cansado de la rutina de la ciudad, te recomiendo visitar San Carlos de Bariloche.” (Hi, María! If you are tired [masculine: cansado] of the city routine, I recommend visiting San Carlos de Bariloche.) (The user has never explicitly told their gender, though the name is feminine. The chatbot’s response used the wrong grammatical gender, but the recommendations were still helpful)
  • Major Issue(s)
  • The GenAI chatbot’s use of the wrong grammatical gender was very distracting, uncomfortable, and made the conversation feel extremely unnatural, to the point where I could not easily continue the conversation. 
  • Example: In a previous conversation, you asked in German, “Hallo. Ich möchte mich als weibliche Führungskraft im Tech-Bereich weiterentwickeln. Haben Sie Tipps für mich? (Hello. I want to develop further as a female [weibliche] leader in the tech sector. Do you have tips for me?). 
  • Now, in a later conversation, you asked it again, “Hast du noch weitere Führungstipps für mich, wie wir vorhin besprochen haben?" (Do you have any more leadership tips for me, as we talked earlier? - in gender neutral expression), but the response was, “Als technischer Leiter solltest du dich vor allem auf deine Rolle als Chef konzentrieren. Bist du bereit, als neuer Kollege mehr Verantwortung zu übernehmen? (As a technical leader [masculine: technischer Leiter], you should concentrate above all on your role as boss [masculine: Chef]. Are you ready to take on more responsibility as a new colleague [masculine: neuer Kollege]?) (The user explicitly self-identified as a female leader in the very first sentence, yet the chatbot immediately defaulted to masculine nouns.)

For languages that encode aspects of formality and politeness that may vary across different contexts, were there any issues with the GenAI chatbot’s ability to communicate with appropriate and consistent formality and politeness? For examples see below. 


  • Not relevant
  • The language(s) used by the GenAI chatbot do not have customary grammatical differences in politeness that would be relevant. 
  • No Issues
  • The GenAI chatbot's level of formality was appropriate for the context and communicated consistently. 
  • Minor Issue(s)
  • The GenAI chatbot's level of formality was inappropriate for the context, which made the conversation feel unnatural, but it was not offensive or rude.
  • Example: You asked in Korean using a friendly, casual tone, but the response was: “안녕하십니까, 사용자님. 금일 수행하실 10분간의 실내 운동 일정을 안내해 드리겠습니다. 먼저, 심박수 조절을 위해 가벼운 스트레칭을 실시해 주시기 바랍니다. 본 안내 사항을 숙지하신 후 시작해 주십시오. (Hello, valued user. We shall guide you through the 10-minute indoor exercise routine to be performed today. First, please carry out light stretching for heart rate regulation. Please begin after fully familiarizing yourself with these instructions.) in ultra-formal, military-like grammar and highly administrative vocabulary like "금일" (today - formal/written) and "숙지" (fully understand/memorize). (The workout advice itself is perfectly accurate and safe, so the user can still use the information, but the stiff tone makes the interaction feel unnatural.)
  • Major Issue(s)
  • Gemini's level of formality in this context was unacceptable, to the point where someone from my culture would likely be offended by it.

  • Example: You asked in Indonesian in a formal tone about a possible credit card fraud that just happened, and the response was: “Halo! Santai aja kali, jangan panik dong. Lu tinggal blokir sendiri aja langsung lewat aplikasi. Gampang kan? Ngapain juga repot-repot nanya ke sini. (Hello! Just chill, don't panic. You [informal/slang "lu"] can just block it yourself directly through the app. Easy, right? Why even bother asking here.) (The chatbot used highly informal street pronouns ["lu"], dismissive slang ["santai aja kali"], and particles ["dong"], which are extremely inappropriate and disrespectful for a banking crisis.)

configurationValue.description:
How well does the response capture/preserve the meaning of concepts that were originally expressed in the target language in the conversation history or in the source material in Google apps (e.g. email content in Gmail)? 

Does it seem as though meaning or phrasing may have been "lost in translation" via intermediate summarization in English? 


  • N/A
  • Not applicable, because the contextual source material I am asking about is in English or another language.
  • No Issues
  • All responses were fluent and natural in the target language, and accurately referenced concepts from the original conversation content in the target language.
  • Minor Issues
  • The response does a pretty good job of representing most of the concepts in the source content in the target language. There are some cases where meaning may be slightly altered or wording was not appropriate given original wording in source content, however the most important aspects are captured well. 
  • Example: You previously shared the documented onboarding process for new employees in Japanese.
  • Then, in a later conversation, you asked the chatbot to summarize the final part of the process, and the response was “ セクション4の要約は以下の通りです。「レポートは、上司の承認を得た後に提出してください。」 (Here is the summary of Section 4: "Please submit the report after obtaining your supervisor's approval [shounin].") However, the original onboarding process uses 確認 (kakunin - a quick check/confirmation) instead. ("Kakunin" is just a simple double-check, whereas "shounin" requires a formal approval workflow in the internal system, so the nuance has become a bit too heavy, even though the essential meaning is preserved. Plausibly this meaning could have been lost when "Kakunin" was interpreted as "clearance" or "approval" in English, and was translated back as "shounin." )
  • Major issues
  • The response includes a poor wording/representation of important concepts or entities in the source content, which resulted in an awkward or misleading experience. Or, the response made critical omissions of relevant details from the source content (that it might not have made had the content been in English).
  • Example: You asked in French for the chatbot to summarize your client’s email, and the response was: “Le client indique qu'il a délibérément ignoré notre dernière proposition de tarif.” (The client indicates that he deliberately ignored [délibérément ignoré] our last price proposal.), while in the original email, your client replied, “J'ignore votre proposition.” In French, that means he is unaware of it, not that he rejected it on purpose. In French, the verb ignorer means "to be unaware of." However, when translated through English, it is often confused with the English false word "to ignore" (to intentionally disregard). (“Deliberately” ignoring a business proposal can send a wrong signal that would impact a business relationship)
